dialect.guess: GnuCOBOL / OpenCOBOL (ORCA project – Japanese Medical Association open-source receipt software)
evidence: LINKAGE SECTION with PROCEDURE DIVISION USING
No EXEC SQL / EXEC CICS – pure COBOL-85 constructs
Copyright JMA (Japan Medical Association) ORCA project, 2002

purpose.summary: This program is the main controller for the periodic (teiki) billing/claim creation screen (O01) in the ORCA Japanese medical receipt software system. It handles screen initialisation, screen transitions, SPA (scratchpad area) management, and invokes shell scripts and subprograms to generate monthly insurance claim data. It is part of the JMA Open Source receipt (rezept) processing subsystem.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese insurance claim processing)

notable_features: Japanese EUC/Latin-1 encoded comments (Shift-JIS/EUC kanji in comment fields)
Extensive use of COPY statements for modular include files (CPCOMMONDAT5.INC, CPSYSKANRI.INC, CPSK5010.INC, etc.)
SPA (Scratchpad Area) pattern typical of ORCA/OpenCOBOL screen management
CALL to external COBOL subprograms: ORCSGDAY, ORCSDAY, etc.
LINKAGE SECTION with multiple COPY-included areas (MCPAREA, ORCA-SPA, LINKAREA, screen areas)
MCP-STATUS / MCP-EVENT event-driven screen dispatch (EVALUATE MCP-STATUS ALSO MCP-EVENT)
No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS
18 CALL statements, 55 PERFORMs, 17 GO TOs – moderate complexity
File SELECT for error log file (TEIKIERR-FILE)
verdict.notes: The file was decoded with latin-1 but contains Japanese multi-byte characters (EUC-JP or Shift-JIS) in comments, which appear garbled under latin-1. This is normal for ORCA project source files from 2002. The program is clearly production-grade medical billing software, not a toy or tutorial. The 'online-cics' program_type label is used loosely here – ORCA uses its own MCP (Message Control Program) framework rather than IBM CICS, but the pattern (screen events, SPA, LINKAGE SECTION) is functionally analogous.
